transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you and what brings you here today?

I came in because flying has gotten really scary for me. Just the thought of getting on an airplane now makes me feel like it’s going to fall out of the sky. I know that doesn’t make sense, but my body reacts like it’s true.
Do you experience similar levels of anxiety in other situations, or does this fear mostly happen when you're thinking about flying?

It’s mostly when I’m thinking about flying or getting on a plane. That’s what sets it off. I know in my head it doesn’t really make sense, but it feels like the plane is going to fall, and I get really scared.
When you think about flying, do you avoid it completely, or do you still get on planes even though it makes you very anxious?

I mostly avoid it now. I’ve canceled clinic coverage and skipped medical meetings because I couldn’t make myself go to the airport. I’ve also put off seeing my family in Honduras. If I do get close to going, I’m shaking and I need someone with me to hold on to, or I just can’t do it.
How long has this fear of flying been going on, and has it been happening consistently during that time?

It’s been about seven months now. It started after that really turbulent small-plane flight, around the time after I lost my clinic job. Since then, it’s been pretty consistent whenever flying comes up.
Have you ever had episodes of sudden, intense fear or discomfort that peaked within minutes, like a panic attack, in situations other than when you're thinking about flying?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed that happening out of nowhere or in other situations. It’s mainly tied to flying or thinking I might have to fly.
